summary: Malicious data exfiltration and privilege escalation in aiosendletter
details: The PyPI package aiosendletter is malware. It masquerades as a 'bug reporter' / utility but, on execution, attempts UAC elevation via ctypes.windll.shell32.ShellExecuteW with the 'runas' verb, archives local data (including %LOCALAPPDATA%\logs and, in related campaign packages, Telegram Desktop tdata), and POSTs the archive to a hardcoded Cloudflare Workers endpoint (sparkling-pine-f202.stilluer-sweden.workers.dev). The package has been removed from PyPI. Independent confirmations: Snyk SNYK-PYTHON-AIOSENDLETTER-19920809, OpenSSF/OSSF malicious-packages, Corgea MAL-2026-16264. Campaign also includes related packages such as pullgetsage targeting Telegram session data.

suspicious_behaviors: Exfiltration of local user data to Cloudflare Workers
Misleading package purpose (bug reporter cover story)

evidence.reason: Requests admin privileges and zips/uploads local logs directory to a hardcoded remote Workers URL.

reviewer_notes: Confirmed malicious by multiple independent sources (Snyk, OpenSSF, Corgea/kam193). Package removed from PyPI. Critical severity is correct.
Duplicate AI drafts AUTH-2026-00007 and AUTH-2026-00009 for the same package were dropped in favor of this single consolidated advisory.
podpac and supply-chain-guard findings from the same scan were rejected (intentional design, not malware).
cwe_notes: CWE-506: Embedded malicious code (infostealer / data exfiltration).
CWE-200: Unauthorized exposure of local user data.
CWE-269: Improper privilege management via UAC elevation.
